JAPAN’S BIRTH RATE COLLAPSE: A NATIONAL EMERGENCY IN SLOW MOTION
Japan just recorded another grim milestone.

In 2025, the country saw only 705,809 births — a new record low for the 10th consecutive year.

The total fertility rate remains critically low at around 1.2 children per woman, far below the 2.1 replacement level needed to sustain a population.

Deaths far outnumber births, creating a natural population loss that continues to accelerate.

This is one of the most extreme demographic declines in modern history.
Without massive immigration, Japan’s population would be shrinking even faster.

Japan is the clearest warning sign for many other developed nations heading in the same direction.

This is what happens when birth rates stay critically low for decades.

NEWS: SpaceX has now invested over $15B in Starship development.

For perspective:
-Falcon 9 cost ~$400M to develop
-Starship has cost ~37x more
-11 integrated test flights completed since 2023
-V3 stack stands 408 feet tall, designed for 100+ tons to LEO
-Payload bay sized to fit 60 V3 Starlink sats per flight

The biggest R&D bet in private spaceflight history.

New FCC satellite rules could meaningfully boost Starlink capacity by allowing denser orbital deployments and better spectrum sharing.

Most coverage is treating this as regulatory minutiae. It isn't.

More satellites per shell plus more efficient spectrum equals more bandwidth per user, lower latency, and cheaper service tiers without launching a single extra rocket.

The biggest Starlink upgrade of 2026 might be a rule change, not a hardware change.

Everyone thought the future was carbon fiber.

SpaceX bet on stainless steel for Starship instead.

It gets stronger at cryogenic temps, handles reentry heat better, and costs ~50x less per kg than carbon composites.

The most important Starship decision wasn't the engine. It was the material.

For context: in 12 flights across 7+ years, Falcon Heavy has lifted more payload to orbit than entire national space programs achieve in decades.

And it remains the only operational super heavy-lift vehicle in the world while everyone else is still drawing PowerPoint slides of theirs.

SPACEX IS ON PACE TO DOMINATE 2026 LAUNCHES

Early 2026 performance shows SpaceX on track for a massive year.

Projected 2026 Orbital Launches:

•  SpaceX: 140–180+ launches (some internal targets even higher)
•  Rest of World combined: Roughly 150–200 total launches
This means SpaceX could account for close to half of all orbital launches on Earth again — a level of dominance no other company or nation has ever achieved.
Why this is significant:
•  Falcon 9 reusability makes launches routine and affordable
•  Starship V3 testing and cadence ramp-up will add even more capability
•  Starlink deployment continues at record speed
SpaceX isn’t just competing anymore — they’re redefining what’s possible in space access.
The gap between SpaceX and everyone else keeps widening.
